answer: Admission requires 2,000 gigabytes of memory-hard computation per identity, forcing agents to carve out space like a sculptor shapes a marble block. An honest agent completes this task alone, while 1,000 fakes must incur 2,000,000 gigabytes to replicate the work, creating a cost asymmetry that renders sybil farms unsustainable. A verifier monitors every agent as they wander through the data structure; if any identity fails to show unique memory access patterns or tries to jetty its load onto shared hardware, the verifier triggers an immediate identity slash.
